text:
Nina (Design): dropping a fresh idea for rollback UI — instead of a full-page modal or side drawer, what about a compact "rollback sheet" that anchors to the timeline row and expands inline? sketch: https://figma.redwood/design/rollback-sheet :sparkles:
Omar (PM): inline sounds less interruptive. main concern: discoverability and preventing accidental rollbacks. how do we surface the risk? :sweat_smile:
Rhea (Design): thinking three layers: 1) inline collapsed sheet with short summary, 2) expand to show config diff + snapshot, 3) final confirm that requires typing the target version number for big changes (>30% traffic). microcopy options attached.
Dev (Eng): implementation note — anchoring to the row is doable but watch z-index with popovers. API needs an idempotency key and a rollback lock to avoid double-submits. also we'll need a server-side guard for cascade rollbacks.
Kai (A11y): for SRs, the sheet should be a region with role="region" and a clear aria-label. When expanded announce: "Rollback sheet opened for version v3.14.2. Undo available for 3 minutes." use aria-live="polite" for the diff summary. avoid flashy visuals.
Ivy (Research): in moderated sessions users preferred inline context — it reduced mis-clicks vs full modals. but people wanted a clear visual boundary. try a subtle elevated card with 1px stroke and 8px radius.
Marco (Data): add event tagging: `rollback_origin` (ui/schedule/api), `traffic_delta`, and `variant_id`. we can compute rollback impact quickly if we capture `requests_per_min` before/after.
Nina (Design): microcopy candidates for the collapsed CTA:
- A: "Open rollback"
- B: "Revert to previous"
- C: "Start rollback (undo available)"
Which is clearer? which is too alarming?
Omar (PM): A is neutral, B is clear, C might scare non-technical users. vote B?
Rhea (Design): my vote B as well. we'll add a short inline hint: "Undo available for 3 minutes" below the CTA in smaller type.
Dev (Eng): perf note: animate height changes with max-height + overflow hidden; avoid layout thrash. also respect prefers-reduced-motion.
Kai (A11y): avoid color-only indicators. for canary badges: use a pill with contrast >=4.5:1 for text and include visually-hidden label like "canary 5%".
Nina (Design): proposal for canary badge states: 
- <10%: yellow dot + text "canary" with aria-label "canary 5 percent"
- 10-50%: orange pill with percent text
- >50%: red pill + "ramping" text
Ivy (Research): micro-test consensus: users read percent numbers, so include explicit "%" next to the value.
Rhea (Design): concern about pulsing for <10% — Kai flagged vestibular issues. suggest static dot + subtle halo on focus only.
Dev (Eng): CSS sample for reduced-motion and focus handling:
```css
.sheet { max-height: 0; transition: max-height 220ms ease; overflow: hidden; }
.sheet.open { max-height: 480px; }
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .sheet, .sheet.open { transition: none; } }
```
Marco (Data): on the A/B we should collect: rollback rate, time-to-rollback, wrong-version errors, clicks on undo. I'll add a dashboard tile.
Nina (Design): confirmation flow: for traffic_delta <=30% — single confirm button (requires clicking). for >30% — require typing the version string (e.g., v3.14.2) into a text field. default keyboard focus should be on "Cancel" so Enter doesn't trigger rollback.
Omar (PM): good safety. also add an inline preview: snapshot timestamp + 3-line config diff (expand to full). reduces fear of unknown changes.
deploy-bot: snapshot uploaded: rollback-sheet-v1.png (sha: b7c2)
Kai (A11y): SR order suggestion: region heading -> version info -> diff summary -> notes textbox -> actions. ensure action buttons have aria-describedby pointing to the diff summary.
Ivy (Research): let's run a 2-arm study: inline sheet vs side drawer with 150 participants (remote moderated) and track task success + perceived safety.
Rhea (Design): decision proposal: 1) Use inline rollback sheet anchored to timeline row. 2) Microcopy: "Revert to previous" for collapsed. 3) Canary badges: static dot with percent text, no pulsing. 4) Confirmation: typed confirm for >30%. 5) Respect prefers-reduced-motion and high-contrast badges. all in favor? :thumbsup:
Omar (PM): +1. schedule a spike and ship to 5% of customers, monitor Marco's metrics for 2 weeks.
Dev (Eng): i'll pick up spike next sprint. will prototype focus behavior and aria attributes.
Nina (Design): I'll update the figma frames and add copy in i18n keys. tagging @Rhea for final review by Wed. thanks everyone! :sparkling_heart:
